transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. Can you start by telling me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Lee, I’m here because... I mean, I was told to come here, mostly because everyone around me keeps acting like this foreclosure on my home is just... just paperwork and missed payments. Like it's some simple administrative thing or a financial mistake. They keep handing me these stacks of documents, highlighting dates and numbers, and looking at me like I just don
When you say it's not just paperwork or missed payments, what do you believe is actually going on with your home and this foreclosure?

Well, Dr. Lee, it’s like I was saying, everyone wants to point at the numbers, but they completely ignore the actual pattern. I mean, you don't just have a series of "clerical errors" that all happen to perfectly align against one person, right? It started almost two years ago. Two whole years! I know exactly what's going on, even if my family just thinks I'm stressed from work or bad at math. 

The bank, the loan servicer... they aren't just making administrative mistakes. They have been quietly working together, coordinating this whole elaborate thing to push me out of my house. And it’s not just the financial institutions, which is the part that no one wants to listen to when I try to explain it. It’s bleeding into my job, too. I'm a supervisor in retail, I manage people, I pay attention to details—I notice when schedules are suddenly shifted to cut my hours the exact same week a mortgage payment is due. I notice when the people at my job start acting strange, whispering, like they know something I don't. They are involved in this. The bank and the people at my job are absolutely working together to force me out of my home. 

And my family, they just bring over these stacks of mail, these foreclosure notices, and say, "Look at the missed payments, look at the dates," but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing with my own two eyes for almost two years. I mean, you can print anything on a piece of paper, right? You can fake a ledger. But you can't fake the way the loan officer wouldn't look me in the eye, or how my manager at the store suddenly started cutting my overtime the exact same week the bank claimed they didn't receive my cashier's check. It’s all connected, it's all orchestrated, and it’s just exhausting trying to explain it to people who only want to look at the surface level of a fake document instead of what's actually happening in the real world...
Aside from noticing these patterns and behaviors, have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you don't seem to hear or see?

No, no, absolutely not. I know exactly why you’re asking that, Dr. Lee, because it’s the exact same thing my sister tried to imply a few months ago when I was trying to show her the discrepancies in the bank statements. She looked at me and asked if I was hearing things. I am not hearing voices, and I am not seeing things that aren't there. I don't have visions. I don't hear ghosts or... or imaginary people talking to me in my head. 

I don't need to hear phantom voices because the actual, real voices of the people doing this are right there in front of me. My hearing is perfectly fine. Actually, it's better than fine—part of being a good floor supervisor is having a good ear. I can hear a cashier giving a customer the wrong return policy from three aisles over, you know? So when I hear my coworkers whispering in the breakroom the second I walk in, or when I hear the loan officer's tone shift on the phone right before they conveniently "drop" my call, I am hearing real things. Real people. 

It’s almost insulting, honestly, that people jump to "she must be hallucinating" just because they don't want to deal with the reality of what's happening. I see my actual manager, David, physically pulling me into the office to tell me my hours are cut again for some made-up payroll reason. I see the actual, physical mail carrier dropping off another supposedly "lost" notice from the bank three weeks after it was dated. I see the way they look at each other when they think I'm not paying attention. It’s all real, tangible stuff. I am completely grounded in reality, which is exactly why this whole orchestrated mess is so incredibly frustrating. I'm wide awake, my eyes work, my ears work, and I only see and hear exactly what they are doing to me in the real world. Nothing more, nothing less.

Outside of these issues with the bank and your job, how would you say you're doing overall—are you keeping up with your usual responsibilities, self-care, and relationships with friends or family the way you used to?

Oh, I'm doing fine. More than fine, honestly, considering everything. I mean, if you take away this whole... this orchestrated nightmare with the foreclosure, I am completely, one hundred percent functional. I get up every single morning at 5:30 AM, like clockwork. I make my coffee, I shower, my clothes are clean and ironed. I go into the store, and I run that floor. I supervise my team, I handle the breaks, the floor schedules—well, the parts of the schedule David hasn't messed with—and I deal with all the customer issues. You know how retail is, right? You get someone screaming in your face about an expired return window, and I handle it calmly and professionally. Every single time. 

I take care of myself. My house—the house they are trying to steal from me—is spotless. I buy groceries, I cook. I still talk to my family, even if my sister gets on my nerves with her whole 'let's look at the math' routine. I still call my mom. Everything in my life, my usual responsibilities... it's all perfectly normal. 

The problems... the only time things get tense or stressful is when they force it on me. The friction mostly starts when I go to the mailbox and there's another thick envelope, or when I get these restricted bank calls right in the middle of my shift, or when David hands me some new, bizarre workplace paperwork that I just know is tied to what I believe is happening with the house. That’s when I have to stop and deal with it, because I have to defend myself. I have to document what they're doing. 

But if it weren't for that? If it weren't for the mail and the calls and the constant maneuvering behind my back? My life would be completely ordinary. I am a very responsible person, Dr. Lee. It's just... it's impossible to just 'go about your day' when you have to constantly look over your shoulder to see how a bank and a retail manager are trying to ruin your life, you know? So my self-care is fine, my relationships are fine, it's just their constant interference that makes things difficult.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre delusional system (~2 years duration) centered on a coordinated conspiracy involving her bank, loan servicer, and workplace to force her out of her home. The delusion is well-systematized, internally consistent, and she cites plausible (if misinterpreted) 'evidence' (mail timing, phone call tone, schedule changes) rather than bizarre or fantastical content. She explicitly denies any hallucinations (auditory or visual), and there is no evidence of disorganized speech, disorganized behavior, or negative symptoms. Functioning outside the delusional theme is preserved—she maintains her job performance, hygiene, household management, and family relationships—arguing against schizophrenia (which requires broader functional decline and typically other Criterion A symptoms) and against a mood disorder with psychotic features (no reported mania or depressive symptoms). The circumscribed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion with preserved functioning outside the delusion is classic for Delusional Disorder (F22).
